question.prompt: What is the x-coordinate of the center of the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x+2y-4=0\)?

solutions.explanation: \(D=-4\), so the x-coordinate of the center is \(-D/2=2\).
solutions.title: Use the center formula

solutions.explanation:
Completing the square makes the center coordinates visible in standard form. Since \(x^2-4x=(x-2)^2-4\) and \(y^2+2y=(y+1)^2-1\), the equation becomes
\[
(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=9.
\]
Its center is \((2,-1)\), so the x-coordinate is \(2\).
solutions.title: Reveal the center in standard form
